text: When taking photographs, aperture and shutter speed are two important elements of the exposure triangle. Aperture refers to the size of the hole in the lens that lets light into the camera. The larger the aperture, the more light that can enter the camera and the shallower the depth of field (the area in focus). Shutter speed, on the other hand, refers to the amount of time the camera's shutter is open. A fast shutter speed can freeze motion, while a slow shutter speed can create motion blur. Understanding the relationship between aperture and shutter speed is essential for creating visually compelling images.
